messages:
aj: quick update from the tessera-13b quant runs — want product/GTN recs before we flip any traffic. ran int8 and int6 bring-ups against our multi-turn summarization and chat slices.

sara: thanks — short summary numbers plz (latency / throughput / quality / rough cost)

miguel: microbench + eval snapshot below. key takeaways first: int8 => ~30% cheaper per-token vs fp16, int6 => ~50% cheaper but quality regresses noticeably on multi-turn summarization slices. p95 latency slightly higher for int6 in long-context due to extra dequant ops.

bench-bot: ```
# run: bench_tool --model tessera-13b --quant int8 --batch 4 --seq 512
int8: p50=120ms p95=310ms toks/sec=72 cost_per_1k_tokens=$0.22
fp16: p50=140ms p95=330ms toks/sec=54 cost_per_1k_tokens=$0.31
int6: p50=110ms p95=420ms toks/sec=95 cost_per_1k_tokens=$0.16
# eval: multi-turn summarization (1000 prompts)
fp16: ROUGE-L=42.1 halluc_rate=3.2%
int8: ROUGE-L=39.8 halluc_rate=6.0%  (drop + +2.8pp halluc)
int6: ROUGE-L=36.5 halluc_rate=9.1%  (big drop)
```

leo: thanks — those hallucination deltas matter for summary product. 6% halluc with int8 will surface as missing facts/omissions in prod.

nina: product note — GTN cares about perceived correctness on summaries; even small factual omissions lead to support tickets. we can tolerate ~2% drift but not 6%.

aj: suggested operational proposal: hybrid routing + canary. short form: route conversational Q/A and non-critical low-risk prompts to int8; keep multi-turn summarization and critical retrieval-to-text on fp16. int6 reserved for cheapest batch workloads (embeddings or non-customer-facing background jobs).

miguel: implementation ideas — add routing rules based on endpoint+signal classifier. proto rule: if endpoint=="/summarize_multi" OR signal.has_long_context==true => fp16. else if request.tokens_predicted < 256 => int8. fallback: if quality metric (signals) crosses threshold send to fp16.

sara: can we quantify unit econ impact of that split? naive calc: 60% traffic -> int8, 30% -> fp16, 10% batch->int6 => weighted cost per 1k tokens = 0.6*0.22 + 0.3*0.31 + 0.1*0.16 = $0.234 => ~25% savings vs all-fp16.

nina: sounds reasonable if we can keep summary reg regressions invisible. need rulebook for the classifier and clear rollback if support metrics spike.

leo: rollout plan: 1) create slice tests (multi-turn summary, long-context chit-chat, factual QA) + automated degraded-quality alert (ROUGE/QA accuracy drift or halluc signal). 2) 10% canary for int8 with shadow traffic to fp16 for summaries for 2 days. 3) if no alerts, 25% for 72h, then 50%. 4) keep immediate fallback per-request if model confidence low.

aj: ops checklist for canary: make sure prompt set includes 200 top GTN queries + 3 long lead-case transcripts; enable tracing to find PII/regression patterns. will draft PR for routing flags.

miguel: one more note — int8 tokenization/generation variability causes a small increase in token counts on some prompts (~+3-5%), factor that into cost forecasts.

sara: OK — can you prepare the canary config + eval slice definition? prefer a single markdown PR that product + GTN can thumb through. nina, can you review the slice selection?

nina: will review today. if we see halluc spike in canary, immediate rollback to fp16 and open a triage. :warning:

aj: great — i'll file the PR and include the bench logs + cost calc. tagging bench-bot to attach raw CSVs. :thumbsup:
